information.description: Visible event IDs available when the forecast was issued.

outcome.description: An unknown outcome is recorded explicitly and is never scored as false.

at.description: When this resolution was recorded, distinct from the outcome's time.

payload_schema.title: CommandExecuted
payload_schema.description:
A command run in a shell, as Atuin recorded it. Atuin updates rows in place
(duration and exit arrive when the command ends; `deleted_at` when the
operator deletes it), so a newer reading with different content replaces
the live one.

duration_ns.description: `None` while the command is still running (Atuin stores -1).

exit_code.description:
`None` while the command is still running. Exit codes are signed: a
signal-killed command is negative.

extra.description: Columns this parser does not know yet, kept by name.

payload_schema.title: CommandImported
payload_schema.description:
A command from a shell's history file: zsh (plain or extended), bash
(with or without `#` timestamp lines) or fish. The source names the shell.
Timed records keep their equivalence key across materials; untimed records use
their material location because neither text nor an unknown start
identifies a record.

started_at.description: Absent in plain history; acquisition time is not a command start.

header_elapsed.description:
zsh's elapsed seconds field as written. With SHARE_HISTORY zsh writes 0
before the command ends, so this is not a duration.

paths.description: The arguments fish recorded as existing paths, in its order.

n.description:
Which record this is among records with the same start second and
command, in file order (the same command run twice in one second is
two runs). Untimed records use their material location instead; this
discriminator is zero and unused for them.
With host, start and command it identifies the timed record
wherever it is read from, so a re-read from the start (a lost position,
bytes stored again) is a repeat, not a new command.

payload_schema.title: WindowFocused
payload_schema.description: A window took keyboard focus.

window.description:
The compositor's window address; `None` when only class and title were
reported before the next event arrived.

payload_schema.title: WindowMoved
payload_schema.description: A window moved to another workspace.

payload_schema.title: DesktopOther
payload_schema.description: A compositor event Sinex has no type for yet, kept whole.

payload_schema.title: NotificationShown
payload_schema.description: A desktop notification was asked for (`org.freedesktop.Notifications.Notify`).

app.description: The application name the sender gave.

replaces_id.description: The notification this one replaces, when the sender gave one.

actions.description: Action identifiers and labels, in the order sent.

hints.description: Hints the sender attached (urgency, category, desktop entry…), as sent.

expire_timeout_ms.description:
How long the sender asked it to stay, in milliseconds (`-1`: the
server decides, `0`: until dismissed).

payload_schema.title: NotificationClosed
payload_schema.description: A notification closed (`NotificationClosed`).

payload_schema.title: NotificationAction
payload_schema.description: The operator picked one of a notification's actions (`ActionInvoked`).

payload_schema.title: ClipboardCopied
payload_schema.description: The clipboard or the primary selection changed.

mime_types.description: The types the owner offered, in its order.

mime_type.description: The type whose content was read.

text.description: The content when it is text; binary content stays in the stored bytes.

content_hash.description: BLAKE3 of the content, so a repeated copy can be recognized.

secret.description:
The owner marked it a secret (a password manager's hint); its content
was not read.

payload_schema.title: PlayerChanged
payload_schema.description:
A media player's state changed (MPRIS `PropertiesChanged`), or was read
when capture started.

player.description:
The player's well-known name (`org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.spotify`) when
known, else its unique bus name.

snapshot.description: `true` when this is the state read at capture start, not a change.

properties.description: Every changed property as sent, decoded from D-Bus types.

payload_schema.title: EditorReport
payload_schema.description: Something the editor reported (a Neovim autocommand).

extra.description: Any other fields the editor sent.

payload_schema.title: TerminalReport
payload_schema.description: Something the terminal reported (a kitty watcher callback).

output.description:
What the command printed, escape sequences removed (`cmd_end` with
kitty's shell integration).

payload_schema.title: MediaSegment
payload_schema.description:
A segment of screen or audio capture: the stored material is the segment
itself (an image or an audio file).

target.description: The output (monitor) or audio target captured.

payload_schema.title: ScreenText
payload_schema.description:
Text read from a screen segment by a local OCR engine. Derived from the
segment's event; recomputed when the engine version changes.

segment.description: The `media.segment` event this text was read from.

payload_schema.title: PageFetched
payload_schema.description:
A page from browser history, fetched by the forward crawl. The stored
material is the response body; a later fetch of the same URL is a newer
reading.

payload_schema.title: WindowSpan
payload_schema.description:
ActivityWatch's window watcher: the focused application and title over a
span. ActivityWatch extends a span in place while the window stays the
same, and the source joins adjacent identical events, so a newer reading
of the span replaces the older one.

span_id.description: The row ID of the first ActivityWatch event in this span.

title.description: The title with animation glyphs removed (see the ActivityWatch source).

merged.description: How many ActivityWatch events this span combines.

payload_schema.title: PresenceSpan
payload_schema.description: ActivityWatch's AFK watcher: whether the operator was at the machine.

payload_schema.title: PresenceInterval
payload_schema.description:
Whether the operator was at the machine over an interval, judged from
ActivityWatch's AFK watcher and corroborating input. The watcher misses idle
transitions under load, so a long not-afk stretch with no input is
`uncertain`, never silently `present`. Derived per logical day by the
presence derivation; the reported spans stay as read.

day.description:
The logical day this interval was computed for (intervals are cut at
day boundaries).

sparse.description:
Present, but with less input than the dense threshold: a real but
quiet stretch (reading, a call), not an artifact.

evidence.description: Corroborating input events inside the interval.

payload_schema.title: BrowserTabActive
payload_schema.description: ActivityWatch's browser watcher: the active tab over a span.

payload_schema.title: ActivityWatchOther
payload_schema.description: An ActivityWatch event from a watcher Sinex has no type for yet, kept whole.

payload_schema.title: WindowSampled
payload_schema.description:
One sample of a window-sampling tracker (arbtt): every open window, which
one was active, and how long input had been idle, taken every `rate_ms`.
The sample's place in the log is its identity.

rate_ms.description: The sampling interval the tracker recorded.

idle_ms.description: Milliseconds since the last keyboard or mouse input.

active_title.description: The active window's title and program, when one was active.

payload_schema.title: JournalEntry
payload_schema.description:
One systemd journal entry. The journal's own cursor identifies it, so an
entry read again (after a capture restart overlaps, or from an export) is
a repeat.

logged_at.description:
`__REALTIME_TIMESTAMP`; `None` when the entry has none or it is malformed
(the time stays unknown rather than becoming the read time).

message.description:
`MESSAGE`; `None` when the journal stored it as binary, which is kept
in `fields` as an array of bytes.

fields.description: Every other field, by its journal name.

CapturePayload.description:
Known fields have concrete types. Unknown lanes or representation kinds
remain explicit; a malformed known field never selects the fallback.

Flow.description:
One network flow record: a connection's endpoints and what it carried
in the producer's sampling interval.

payload_schema.title: FileChanged
payload_schema.description: A change to a watched file or directory, as the kernel reported it.

change.description:
`created`, `modified`, `written` (closed after writing), `removed`,
`renamed`, `moved_from`, `moved_to`, `attributes`, `other`, or
`unwatched` (the kernel refused a watch on this directory; see `note`).

path.description: The path, when it is UTF-8 (otherwise see `path_hex`).

path_hex.description: The path's bytes in hex, when they are not UTF-8.

to.description: The new path, for a rename that reported both ends.

payload_schema.title: TerminalSession
payload_schema.description:
A terminal recording's session (asciinema): its start, size, command and
environment, from the recording's header. The recording's place is its
identity.

header.description: The header as recorded (terminal type, theme, environment).

payload_schema.title: TerminalOutput
payload_schema.description:
A span of a terminal recording, as plain text with escape sequences
removed: one shell command's output where the recording kept input. A span
starts at a typed Enter, so it holds the command's output, the next prompt
and the next command line as typed up to its own Enter; it also ends at a
size bound, a resize or the exit. The cast stays whole as the material,
and the span's record is its exact byte range there, so the original
stream is replayable from the material; per-event detail is a read over
it.

output.description:
What was written to the terminal (`o` events), escape sequences
removed.

input.description: What was typed (`i` events), when the recording kept input.

resize.description: The last resize (`r`) or the exit status (`x`) the span ends with.

payload_schema.title: ScrollbackCaptured
payload_schema.description:
What a kitty window's scrollback held when it was captured: a snapshot in
the Sinnix lake (`kitty @ get-text`, every window on a timer), or the kitty
integration's capture of a window's new lines on a cadence and when it
closes. `text` holds only the lines new since the previous capture of the
same window, escape sequences removed; the stored material keeps the
capture as taken.

kitty_pid.description: The kitty process; absent in older lake snapshots.

title.description:
The window's title; for a lake snapshot, as its file name spells it
(the sidecar's `scrollback.window` has it exactly).

lines.description: Lines the window held at capture, scrollback and screen.

continues.description:
Whether `text` continues the previous capture of this window. False for
a window's first capture, and when the previous capture is not where
this one starts (the window was cleared, or resized and its lines
wrapped again): `text` is then the whole capture.

payload_schema.title: ScrollbackWindow
payload_schema.description:
The window a lake scrollback snapshot was taken of, from the snapshot's
sidecar file: kitty's title and working directory at capture.

extra.description: Any other fields the sidecar has.

payload_schema.title: KeyPressed
payload_schema.description: A key went down, or repeated while held.

session.description: The logger process that wrote the record, one per input device.

logged_at.description: When the logger wrote the record (milliseconds).

kernel_at.description:
The kernel's time of the key event (microseconds): the keystroke's own
timing. Older logs do not have it. The logger's time can trail it by
seconds when the pipeline backs up.

key.description:
The key's name as the logger wrote it (`KEY_A`, or `KEY_106` when it
had no name for the code).

code.description: The kernel's key code; absent in older logs.

value.description:
The kernel's value: 1 pressed, 2 repeated while held; absent in older
logs, which logged presses only.

changed.description: Whether the key changed the logger's typed-text buffer.

clipboard.description: The clipboard text the logger read when the key was a paste.

window.description: The focused window, as older logs recorded it.

extra.description: Fields this parser does not know yet, kept by name.

payload_schema.title: KeyReleased
payload_schema.description: A key went up.

kernel_at.description: The kernel's time of the key event; see [`KeyPressed::kernel_at`].

payload_schema.title: PointerButton
payload_schema.description:
A pointer button went down or up. The logger records no kernel time for
pointer records, so the time is the logger's.

value.description: The kernel's value as logged (1 down, 0 up).

payload_schema.title: PointerMoved
payload_schema.description:
The pointer moved along one axis: a relative step (`REL_X`, `REL_Y`) or an
absolute position (`ABS_X`, a tablet's).

value.description: The step (relative axes) or the position (absolute axes).

payload_schema.title: PointerScrolled
payload_schema.description:
A scroll wheel turned: `REL_WHEEL` and `REL_HWHEEL` in detents,
`REL_WHEEL_HI_RES` and `REL_HWHEEL_HI_RES` in 1/120 of one.

payload_schema.title: InputLogger
payload_schema.description:
A record about the logger itself (`start`, `stop`, a `focus` change in
older logs, a typed-text `snapshot`), or one of a kind this parser has no
type for, with its fields as written.

payload_schema.title: GitCommit
payload_schema.description:
One commit. A commit never changes once made; its ID is its identity, so
seeing it again (another ref, another clone at the same path) is a repeat.

repository.description: The repository's working directory (or git directory, when bare).

message.description: The full message, decoded lossily when it is not UTF-8.

refs.description: The refs that pointed at this commit when it was first read.

payload_schema.title: CommandFused
payload_schema.description:
One command run, from Atuin and zsh history. zsh history holds about a
thousand pairs of the same command in the same second on the operator's
machine, which is why the record, not the text and time, identifies it.

record.description:
The preferred member's identity: `<type>:<native id>` when the source
has one (Atuin), otherwise its record location.

observed_by.description: The sources that observed this command.

payload_schema.title: FocusFused
payload_schema.description:
A stretch during which a window had keyboard focus, from the compositor's
focus changes and ActivityWatch's window spans. Focus is exclusive, so
whatever the sources call the window, two of them seeing focus begin at
the same moment saw the same focus.

app.description: The application: the compositor's window class or ActivityWatch's app.

payload_schema.title: VisitFused
payload_schema.description:
One page visit, from a browser's own history, a Takeout history export
and the browser-navigation capture.

payload_schema.title: PlayFused
payload_schema.description:
One play of a track, from a streaming history export and the media
player's live state (live MPRIS capture and the capture lake).

player.description: The player that reported it, when a live source saw it.

ended_at.description: When playback stopped, or the track's end when only its length is known.

payload_schema.title: ClipboardFused
payload_schema.description:
One clipboard or primary-selection change, from live capture and the
capture lake.

payload_schema.title: NotificationFused
payload_schema.description: One desktop notification, from live capture and the capture lake.

payload_schema.title: MailFused
payload_schema.description:
One mail message, from every mail source that holds it (IMAP, Maildir,
mbox, Outlook): its `Message-ID` and `Date` are the same wherever it is
stored.

payload_schema.title: ShellSession
payload_schema.description:
A run of shell commands on one host with no gap longer than the session
rule's gap between one command's end and the next command's start. Derived
from fused commands; identified by host and start (its end moves as it
grows; its start does not), so a session that grows replaces its earlier reading.

ended_at.description:
The latest recorded end of any member command (a command without a
duration counts as a point).

day.description: The logical day the session belongs to (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

payload_schema.title: StateInterval
payload_schema.description:
A span during which some state held: a focused window, a workspace, an
ActivityWatch bout. Derived from transitions by the
interval derivation. Identified by its start evidence; the end may still
be unknown (`ended_at` is `None` while the state holds).

interval_id.description: `<state kind>:<subject>:<start record location or start time>`.

end_event_type.description:
What ended it: the next transition, a fence, a stop, or the observed
duration (`None` while open).

payload_schema.title: MetricFigure
payload_schema.description:
One metric over one civil hour or logical day: how many input events it
counted and the metric's number for them, in total or for one value of a
breakdown field. Hourly figures are computed from the metric's input
events, daily ones from the day's hourly figures. A period nothing was
counted in has no figure; whether that means zero or unobserved depends on
whether the sources were observing, which is read with the figures.

day.description: The logical day the period belongs to (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

dimension.description:
The breakdown field (`cwd`), and the value this figure counts for;
both empty for the total.

value.description:
The metric's number; `None` where it is undefined (a ratio of zero
commands with a known exit code).

numerator.description: A ratio's parts, summed from hours to the day.

payload_schema.title: HealthFigure
payload_schema.description:
Figures over one series of health points in one civil hour or logical
day: how many points started in the period and, for each numeric value
position, their count, sum, minimum and maximum. Hourly figures are
computed from the points, daily ones from the day's hourly figures.

day.description: The logical day the period belongs to (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

series.description: Where the points came from: a Fit data source.

FigureValue.description: One numeric value position of a series' points, over a period.

payload_schema.title: BrowserVisit
payload_schema.description:
One visit in a Chromium-family browser's `History` database (`visits`
joined with `urls`). Chromium writes the visit when it starts and fills in
its duration when the page is left, so a newer reading replaces the live
one.

url.description: `None` when the visit's `urls` row is gone.

from_visit.description: The visit this one came from (a link click); `None` when it had none.

transition.description:
Chromium's page transition as stored: the core type in the low byte,
transition flags above it.

duration_us.description: How long the page stayed open; `None` while it is still open (0).

extra.description: Columns this parser does not know yet, kept by name.

payload_schema.title: BrowserUrl
payload_schema.description:
One row of a Chromium-family browser's `urls` table: a page and its
running counts, updated in place as it is visited again.

payload_schema.title: BrowserHistoryEntry
payload_schema.description:
One entry of a Google Takeout Chrome history export. It has no ID, so the
URL and time identify it, and a later export of the same entry is a repeat.

client_id.description: The synced device the visit came from.

payload_schema.title: MusicPlayed
payload_schema.description:
One play of a track, episode or audiobook chapter from a Spotify streaming
history export. Spotify records when playback stopped (`ts`, or `endTime`
in the older account-data export) and how long it played; the start is
derived from those two.

skipped.description: Spotify's own skip flag; `None` when the export does not say.

extra.description:
Fields this parser does not model (`ip_addr`, `offline_timestamp`, new
fields), kept by name.

payload_schema.title: BookmarkSaved
payload_schema.description:
A saved bookmark in a bookmarking service (Raindrop). The service's ID is
the identity, so an edited or moved bookmark is a newer reading; one in the
trash is removed at the source.

folder.description: The collection or folder it is filed in.

highlights.description: Highlighted passages, as the service exported them.

trashed_at.description:
When it went to the trash. The trash export gives no time, so the last
update stands for it.

payload_schema.title: NoteDocument
payload_schema.description:
A note file in a notes vault (Obsidian, plain Markdown folders). The vault
and the path inside it identify it; an edit is a newer reading, and a file
missing from a completed scan is removed at the source.

text.description: The file's text; `None` for a removed file.

removed_at.description: When a completed scan first found the file gone.

title.description: Absent for a removed file and for a note without one.

note_id.description: The exact front-matter string, including an explicitly empty ID.

tags.description:
Sorted string tags from the parsed header and known body. An invalid
front_matter means header tags remain unknown.

NoteFrontMatter.description: The parsed YAML header, separate from the exact original note text.

line.description: One-based coordinates in the note, when the parser supplies them.

NoteFrontMatterError.description: Structural diagnostics contain no copied note text or YAML snippets.

payload_schema.title: ChatMessage
payload_schema.description:
One line of a chat log (WeeChat IRC logs): a message, an action, or a
join, part, quit or other notice. Logs have no message IDs and only grow, so
the record location is the identity.

nick.description: The sender's nick, without its mode prefix.

prefix.description: The mode prefix shown before the nick (`@`, `+`), if any.

oneOf.description: Server and client lines without a sender.

payload_schema.title: MailMessage
payload_schema.description:
One email message, from an mbox file or a Maildir. The `Message-ID` header
identifies it (a hash of the raw message when the header is missing), and a
later export with different labels is a newer reading.

date.description: The `Date` header; `None` when missing or unreadable.

html_only.description: True when the message has HTML but no plain text part.

size.description: The raw message's size in bytes.

payload_schema.title: ActionRecorded
payload_schema.description:
One entry of an account's activity log (Google My Activity): a search, a
visit, an app action. The instant is the identity across exports: each
export writes its times in the zone of the export day, and restates titles,
so neither the time text nor the title can be.

verb.description:
The words before the link (`Searched for`, `Visited`); a field, never
part of the identity, since Google rewords it between exports.

title.description: The linked text, or the whole first line when nothing is linked.

unlinked_text.description:
For an entry without a link, its first line; the identity then rests
on it beside the instant, so two unlinked actions in one second stay
apart.

lines.description: Lines between the title and the time.

zone_label.description:
The time zone label the export printed (`UTC`, `CEST`); the export
day's zone, kept for reference.

payload_schema.title: VideoWatched
payload_schema.description: A video watched on a video service (YouTube watch history).

video_id.description:
`None` when the entry links no video: a removed video Google lists
without a link, or a link to something other than a video.

title.description:
`None` when the export names no title: the video is gone and Google
writes `Watched <url>`. A later export that drops a title an earlier
one had does not erase it (`keep_known`).

payload_schema.title: VideoSearched
payload_schema.description: A search on a video service (YouTube search history).

payload_schema.title: NoteObserved
payload_schema.description:
A note kept in a notes service (Google Keep). Keep writes no note ID and
names files after titles, so the creation time is the identity; a later
edit is a newer reading.

trashed_at.description:
The edit time when the note is in the trash; the export gives no time
of trashing.

attachments.description: Attached files, by the name Takeout wrote them under.

payload_schema.title: TaskRevised
payload_schema.description:
A task in a task list (Google Tasks); a later export's reading with a newer
`updated` replaces it.

payload_schema.title: PurchaseObserved
payload_schema.description:
An order, install, library item or purchase an account store recorded
(Google Play, Purchases). The time is the wrapped item's own field.

record_kind.description:
The wrapper the item came in: `orderHistory`, `install`,
`purchaseHistory`, `libraryDoc`.

native_id.description: The provider's ID, or a hash of the item when it has none.

payload_schema.title: CalendarEvent
payload_schema.description:
One event of a calendar (RFC 5545 `VEVENT`), from an export or a calendar
API. A recurring series is one event with its rule; a changed occurrence is
its own event with a recurrence ID. Expanding a rule into occurrences is a
derivation.

calendar.description: The calendar it belongs to (the export's calendar name).

recurrence_id.description:
For one changed occurrence of a series, the original start it replaces,
as written.

all_day.description: A date without a time: the event spans whole days.

zone.description:
The zone the times were written in (`Europe/Warsaw`, `UTC`), or
`floating` for local times the export ties to no zone, read in the
configured zone.

cancelled_at.description: The last-modified time when the status is `CANCELLED`.

extra.description: Properties not modelled above, by name, as written.

payload_schema.title: LocationSample
payload_schema.description:
A location fix an account recorded (Google Location History): where the
device was, how sure it was, and what it thought the operator was doing.
The device and the instant identify it across exports.

device.description: The export's device tag; `None` in older exports, which carry none.

accuracy_m.description: Meters, as the provider reported it.

activity.description: Activity guesses with their confidences, as exported.

payload_schema.title: ConversationMessage
payload_schema.description:
A message in a direct or group conversation of a messaging service
(Facebook Messenger, SMS). Exports carry no thread or message ID that
survives between them, so a message is the thread (its participants), its
time and its sender; the same message read from another export or input is
the same occurrence.

thread.description: The thread's participants, sorted and joined by `|`.

thread_name.description: The name the export gave the thread.

media.description: Media and attachments, by the path the export wrote them under.

message_id.description: The service's message ID, when the export has one.

unsent_at.description:
When the sender unsent it; the export gives no time, so the send time
stands for it.

payload_schema.title: BookStatus
payload_schema.description:
A book shelved or read in a reading tracker (Goodreads). Dates are days,
so these serve long-horizon interest, not daily behaviour.

at.description: The day, at midnight UTC; the export gives no time of day.

my_rating.description: The operator's rating, 1-5; `None` when unrated (the export writes 0).

HealthValues.description:
Known source categories select their fields before decoding. A malformed
known field is an error, never a reason to read the row as unknown.

Scalar.description: CSV normalization preserves numbers and numeric-looking text separately.

Binning.description: A companion-file reference, decoded source bins, or an unrecognized object.

HealthEvent.description: In-session markers keep their source order and nullable numeric value.

payload_schema.title: PostPublished
payload_schema.description: A post, comment or link the operator published.

parent.description: What it replies to or belongs to (the entry or link a comment is on).

community.description: The community or tags it was filed under.

payload_schema.title: VoteCast
payload_schema.description:
A vote the operator cast on someone's post. Exports list votes without the
time they were cast, so the event time is unknown; the target's own time is
a field.

withdrawn_at.description: Set when the export records the vote as withdrawn (Reddit's `none`).

payload_schema.title: NotificationReceived
payload_schema.description:
A notification an online community sent the operator (Wykop: a new entry
or link under a tag the operator observes). The service's notification ID
is the identity; a later reading that marks it read is newer.

target.description: What it points at, as `entry:<id>` or `link:<id>`.

channel.description: The tag or channel it came through.

payload_schema.title: AccountSetting
LogEntry
payload_schema.description:
One entry of the operator's quick-note log. The entry is its place in the
log; an edit to it is a newer reading.

written_at.description:
Unknown for an entry headed by a label instead of a time
(`**SPECIAL:**`).

label.description: The bold heading when it is a label, not a time.

text.description: The entry's text, continuation lines included.

payload_schema.title: SteeringRow
payload_schema.description:
One steering row, identified by its table and record ID, with typed known
values.

SteeringValues.description:
A closed choice of known row shapes. Deserialization is selected by the table,
never by trying these variants against the same untagged object.

Commitment.description: A commitment and forecast, including the written outcome.

Activity.description: An undated activity or experiment in the steering catalog.

Review.description: The written review; generated_summary remains model output.

payload_schema.title: FileCopy
payload_schema.description:
A file seen in a library root by a scan. Identified by host and path: a
changed file is a newer reading, a file missing from a completed scan is
removed at the source. The bytes are named by `content` whether or not the
scan kept them.

root.description: The library root the scan walked.

content.description: `blake3:<hex>`, the content store's name for the bytes.

sha256.description: Hex digests other catalogues name files by (Hydrus, boorus).

media_type.description:
Sniffed from the bytes; `application/octet-stream` when unknown. A file
Sinex cannot read is still stored and described.

stored.description:
Whether the scan stored the bytes in the content store (a root can be
indexed by reference only).

moved_from.description:
The path this file had before: the same file (device and inode) with
the same bytes was seen there by an earlier walk. Evidence of a rename.

previous_content.description:
The bytes this path held before, when the same file changed in place.
Evidence that an item continued with new bytes.

vanished_at.description: When a completed scan first found the file gone.

payload_schema.title: Item
payload_schema.description:
One revision of an item. The live reading is the current revision; the
archived readings are its history. New bytes make a new revision only
when continuity was shown (a library operation, or the same file changing
in place); an unrelated copy of the same bytes is a different item.

item.description: Opaque: independent of digests, paths, labels and event IDs.

copies.description: Copies that belong to the item, as `host:path`.

label.description: A human label; the file name at intake when nothing better is known.

payload_schema.title: Rendition
payload_schema.description:
Bytes standing for an item revision: its original, or something made
from it. A preview never answers a request for the original.

made_from.description: The rendition it was made from; `None` for an original.

made_with.description: How it was made: the tool and its settings.

payload_schema.title: Assignment
payload_schema.description:
One value given to one field of a target: a tag (`field = "tag"`), or a
property. A property can be set to empty (`value = None`), which stops
fallback to lower levels. Withdrawing an assignment is a newer reading of
it with `withdrawn_at` set.

source_ref.description: Where an imported value came from: a sidecar file, a post URL.

Target.description:
What an assignment, entry or view is about: an item (following its
revisions), one revision, one rendition, or a part of a rendition.

part.description:
A selector inside the rendition: `t=12.5-40` (seconds, half-open) or
`xywh=10,10,200,120` (pixels).

Level.description: Who an assigned value comes from, highest first in the selection policy.

oneOf.description: The operator's own value; wins over everything, an empty one included.
Brought in from another application or site.

payload_schema.title: Collection
payload_schema.description:
A collection: an ordered list of entries, optionally with a saved query that
offers suggestions. A fixed selection is a collection without a query whose
entries were added from a query's results.

selected_from.description: The query the entries were selected from, for a fixed selection.

payload_schema.title: Entry
payload_schema.description:
One entry in a collection. Each insertion is a new entry, so the same item
can appear twice; removing an entry withdraws it and keeps it inspectable.

target.description: The item, with the revision fixed when it was added.

position.description:
Sort position; an entry inserted between two takes a value between
theirs.

Target.description:
What an assignment, entry or view is about: an item (following its
revisions), one revision, one rendition, or a part of a rendition.

part.description:
A selector inside the rendition: `t=12.5-40` (seconds, half-open) or
`xywh=10,10,200,120` (pixels).

payload_schema.title: Rating
payload_schema.description: A rating on a named scale (`stars`, `favourite`), one per rater.

of.description: The top of the scale (5 stars, 1 for a like).

Level.description: Who an assigned value comes from, highest first in the selection policy.

oneOf.description: The operator's own value; wins over everything, an empty one included.
Brought in from another application or site.

payload_schema.title: Comparison
payload_schema.description:
One pairwise judgement: `winner` is better than `loser` on `scale`. A
ranking is fitted from all of them.

payload_schema.title: View
payload_schema.description:
One time something was opened for viewing or playing. The target is fixed
when the request is made.

player.description: The program it was handed to.

seconds.description: How long it was open; `None` while it still is, or when unknown.

count.description: Imported view counts carry how many views the record stands for.

What an assignment, entry or view is about: an item (following its
revisions), one revision, one rendition, or a part of a rendition.

part.description:
A selector inside the rendition: `t=12.5-40` (seconds, half-open) or
`xywh=10,10,200,120` (pixels).

Level.description: Who an assigned value comes from, highest first in the selection policy.

oneOf.description: The operator's own value; wins over everything, an empty one included.
Brought in from another application or site.

payload_schema.title: Dismissal
payload_schema.description:
A collection suggestion the operator dismissed; remembered for that
collection and query revision.

query.description: The saved query's text when the suggestion was seen.
